key_insight: The study shows that optimized metallic microstructure and texture can be used to infer the likely alloy recipe and processing conditions, with conventional descriptors outperforming learned embeddings on this small magnesium extrusion dataset.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven route to reverse-engineer manufacturing settings from desired microstructures, supporting faster alloy/process selection in design and troubleshooting.
method: Compared three representations of microstructure/texture: hand-crafted grain/texture statistics, pretrained vision embeddings, and a graph neural network on grain networks.
Paired each descriptor with two prediction tasks: infer alloy composition from process conditions, and infer process parameters from composition.
Compared free regression heads with discrete, ordered classification heads for limited recipe/process options.
evidence_signal: On 107 extrusion conditions across 14 magnesium alloys with optical micrographs and X-ray texture data, 5-fold cross-validation showed conventional descriptors correctly identified the alloy 65% of the time, versus 17% for always predicting the most common alloy, while learned embeddings stayed below 30% and microstructure roughly halved temperature error for process prediction.
watch_item: The dataset is small and discrete in both alloys and press settings, so results may not generalize well beyond the specific in-house conditions and the ordered-classification design.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
